ocrComparator.label: FIXED SYNTHETIC DEVELOPMENT OCR COMPARATOR — NOT HISTORICAL PRODUCTION CONFIGURATION

transport.credentialsReadBy: proxy only, from OPENROUTER_API_KEY and OPENROUTER_BASE_URL

criteriaPath.note: Routed through the same bounded proxy under its own stage label.

requestCount.mechanism: proxy request slot taken before forwarding; check and increment are synchronous in one task
requestCount.provedBy: proxy-audit.test.mjs: exact ceiling, concurrent cap, per-stage independence

tokens.mechanism: atomic reservation of the maximum permitted request cost (20000 in + 4000 out) before forwarding; reservation released to reported usage on completion
tokens.aggregateRule: chargedInput + reservedInput + newReservation <= stage input cap (same for output)
tokens.inputGuard: serialized body bytes <= 20000. Every token covers at least one byte, so bodyBytes <= 20000 proves tokenCount <= 20000. This is a provable bound, not an estimate; chars/4 exists only as an offline convenience and must not be used for a live run.
tokens.inputBoundConsequence: a byte bound is roughly 4x tighter than a 20,000-token ceiling
tokens.outputCeiling: max_output_tokens injected as 4000 when absent; a caller-declared value above 4000 is refused at 413, never clamped
tokens.policyPin: model, service_tier and reasoning.effort are pinned; any other value is refused at 400 with no forward

inBinaryMaxTokensBudget.metric: combined input + output tokens (agent TotalTokensUsed), compared against the budget
inBinaryMaxTokensBudget.checkPoint: before each review round, not before each request
inBinaryMaxTokensBudget.overshoot: one final round may be allowed after the threshold is crossed, so this is a secondary brake and NOT a hard bound
inBinaryMaxTokensBudget.cacheTokens: cache read/write counters exist separately and are not part of the compared metric
inBinaryMaxTokensBudget.role: secondary guard; the proxy reservation is the hard bound

providerSideBypass.hardUsdGuaranteeCondition: key limit set to USD 1.00 at the provider, so a proxy defect cannot exceed the ceiling

accounting.perRequestLedger: JSONL: stage, decision, model, tier, effort, estimates, reported usage, charged tokens, halt state, running totals
accounting.chargingPolicy: reported usage when present; otherwise the full reservation. Never zero, never a floor.
accounting.cacheHandling: usage.input_tokens is charged at the full input rate (no cache discount assumed); usage.output_tokens includes reasoning tokens
accounting.authoritativeReconciliation: GET https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/key usage delta before and after each stage

retryPolicy.binaryInternalRetries: present (llm.RetryReport); each attempt is a separate HTTP request and therefore consumes a proxy slot
retryPolicy.retryAfterHalt: refused at 402; a halt cannot be retried through the proxy

stopRules: any request refused by the request cap or the token reservation
any 4xx, refusal, malformed or contract-invalid response
any response without usage (cost unknowable) — halt immediately
any timeout or transport error after forwarding — halt immediately
credential absent from the Agent process, or present in any artifact
a policy-pinned model, tier or effort mismatch on any forwarded request

correctionWorkflow.authorized: manual correction by the operator, then the same OCR and criteria stages
correctionWorkflow.codingAgentInference: NOT authorized and NOT counted in this budget: Freebuff's own inference cannot be routed through or measured by this proxy
correctionWorkflow.reviewerReportAndDecisionCheckpoint: unchanged (one advisory report, one recorded human decision, then one recheck)

knownLimitations: The proxy cannot prove the pinned binary never opens a second egress. Managed mode rejects a non-loopback provider URL and the proxy is the only credentialed component, so no path is known; a container with no default route would make this structural.
Request count is exact; token cost is exact only where the provider reports usage. When usage is absent the run halts rather than estimating.
The in-binary --max-tokens-budget can overshoot by one round, so it is a brake, not the bound.
A proxy defect could still leave the provider bill above USD 1.00 unless the key limit is lowered to USD 1.00.

The provable input bound is 20,000 bytes. This fixture's theoretical maximal single prompt (all tracked files 12,793 + requirements 1,766 + background at its 8,000-char cap) is 22,559 bytes, so a maximal prompt would be refused and the run would halt safely. Exact token-level enforcement at the approved 20,000-token width needs a tokenizer.
The M2 Profile A adapter already caps rendered reviewer input at 8,000 characters before dispatch, so ordinary requests are expected to fit well inside the byte bound.
